summary: This Dockerfile creates a PHP 8.2 container with Chrome browser and ChromeDriver installed for testing purposes. It sets up a non-root user with matching host machine permissions, installs system dependencies and Chrome from Google's repositories, downloads a specific Chrome version and its driver, and prepares a working directory for Behat tests.

explanations.3: ARG declares a build-time variable that can be passed when building the image; DOCKER_UID will default to 1000 if not specified.
explanations.19: These ARG lines re-declare the variables so they're available in this build stage; Docker requires you to redeclare ARG variables after certain commands if you want to use them later.
explanations.23: This creates a system group with the specified group ID, using the username as the group name.
explanations.24: This creates a new user account with a home directory, matching the host machine's user ID and group ID so file permissions stay consistent between container and host.
explanations.29: This ARG sets the URL to Google's JSON file that lists all available Chrome versions and their download locations.
explanations.32: This downloads Google's public key and adds it to the system's trusted keys so the system can verify Chrome packages are legitimate.
explanations.45: This runs curl to fetch the JSON file, then uses jq to parse it and find the download URL for the exact Chrome version specified, filtering for the linux64 platform.
explanations.49: The -j flag tells unzip to extract files directly into the destination folder without creating a subfolder, keeping the directory structure flat.
explanations.54: Similar to line 45, this fetches and extracts the ChromeDriver URL from the same JSON file, but this time for the driver instead of the browser.
explanations.65: COPY --from pulls the composer executable from the official composer Docker image and adds it to this image, avoiding the need to download and install it ourselves.
